selector_result.evaluation_process: Q1 fills in the time boundary of the plan (single week, fixed multi-week, or indefinite until tasks complete), which is critical because wages, effective hours, and worker caps are all expressed per week and the planning horizon determines how they aggregate. Q2 fills in the decision scope for method selection, clarifying whether each task uses exactly one method or can mix methods. Q3 fills in the hard/soft policy for worker maximums, clarifying whether the 400/800 caps apply per week, per task, or over the whole plan. All three address open gaps and reduce silent-assumption risk. However, Q1 is the most foundational: without a confirmed planning horizon, the model cannot correctly interpret weekly wages, weekly effective hours, or the worker caps, and the Agent would otherwise silently assume a horizon. Q2 and Q3 are also important, but their correct interpretation depends on the time boundary. Therefore Q1 best reduces pre-modeling silent-assumption risk.

This is a core modeling structure that determines whether method choice is a single discrete selection per task or a continuous allocation, and it directly affects the feasible set and cost calculation. Q2 fills in the hard/soft policy gap G003 about whether worker caps apply per week, per task, or to total hires; this is important but somewhat less foundational than method-choice structure because the single-week horizon already narrows the interpretation. Q3 fills in the entity-relation gap G004 about worker sharing across tasks; this is also important, but it is a secondary assignment detail that depends on how tasks and methods are structured. Q1 is the best first question because it resolves the most fundamental decision-scope ambiguity, prevents the Agent from silently assuming either one-method-per-task or mixed-method allocation, and its options are clear, mutually exclusive, and answerable by a business user.

selector_result.evaluation_process: Q1 asks whether a hired worker can be assigned to more than one task during the week. This fills in a core decision-scope and entity-assignment rule: whether workers are task-dedicated or pooled across tasks. It directly addresses the only unresolved business assumption in C1/C2/C3 and would prevent the Agent from silently assuming a worker-to-task assignment structure. Q2 asks whether a worker's full weekly effective hours must be used on the assigned task; this is related but narrower and partly presupposes the answer to Q1. Q3 asks how required workers are determined for Task 2 Method A and Task 3 Method A; this is more mathematically salient and concerns hour-contribution mechanics rather than the main unresolved business rule. Q1 is the best choice because it resolves the key open business-structure gap and reduces silent-assumption risk most directly.

selector_result.evaluation_process: Q1 targets G003, clarifying whether the 400/800 worker maximums are weekly totals, per-task limits, or horizon totals. This is a hard/soft policy and scope boundary that directly changes the feasible region and hiring decisions. Q2 targets G006/G012, clarifying whether the 60% skilled-to-laborer ratio compares hired or assigned counts; this is also important but somewhat narrower and partly overlaps with Q1's hiring-vs-assignment distinction. Q3 targets G007, clarifying whether conditional method restrictions are hard or soft; this is relevant but less immediately structural than the worker-cap scope because the conditional restrictions are already stated as rules and the main ambiguity is enforcement. Q1 best reduces silent-assumption risk because the model must otherwise assume whether caps bind per week, per task, or over the horizon, which materially affects the objective and decision scope. Its options are clear, mutually exclusive, and answerable by a business user.

selector_result.evaluation_process: Q1 fills in whether the 60% skilled-to-laborer ratio is a hard constraint or soft target (G013), which directly affects the feasible region and objective formulation. Q2 fills in whether the 400/800 worker maximums are hard caps or soft limits (G014), also a hard-versus-soft policy that changes constraints and possible penalties. Q3 fills in whether the 20-skilled minimum for Task 3 Method B is additional to the group ratio or implied by it (G016), which affects constraint structure but is narrower and more conditional. Among these, Q1 addresses the most broadly binding policy: the 60% ratio applies to total hiring and can materially change the optimal hiring mix and cost objective. It is not merely mathematically salient; it is a core business rule whose ambiguity would otherwise force the Agent to silently assume hard or soft treatment. Q2 is also important, but caps are more naturally treated as hard limits and less likely to alter the objective structure. Q3 is more local and conditional. Therefore Q1 best reduces pre-modeling silent-assumption risk.
